title: Enterprise procurement behavior scenarios and adoption barriers matrix
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Synthesize qualitative and quantitative signals into a set of enterprise procurement behavior scenarios that explain how customers decide between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Produce a matrix of adoption barriers and seller tactics (pricing, SLAs, proofs-of-concept, compliance artifacts) that map to each scenario so sales and PM can tailor engagement plays.
goals: Create 6 empirically grounded procurement scenarios for mid-market and enterprise buyers
Map key friction points (latency tolerance, data governance, procurement cycles, vendor lock-in concerns) to decision triggers
Produce an actionable seller play matrix listing 3 prioritized interventions per scenario
Deliver a one-page field cheat-sheet + an artifact library (SLA language, security checklist, pilot template)
background: We have many market signals showing customers trade latency vs cost vs control, but the team lacks a consolidated view that connects observed procurement behaviors with pragmatic seller actions. Existing model-supply and fallback workstreams capture supply-side risk; this ticket captures demand-side decision heuristics to reduce friction when offering hosted, dedicated, and private options.
hypotheses: H1: Customers with strict compliance requirements prefer private deployments, but procurement speed is driven more by pre-built compliance artifacts than technical deployment time
H2: Latency-sensitive buyers choose dedicated capacity if predictable tail latency is proven; otherwise they default to host with higher-cost SLAs
H3: Small-mid enterprises are most sensitive to upfront integration effort; a low-effort POC reduces time-to-decision more than a discount
H4: Quantization or model variant complexity increases perceived migration risk and extends procurement cycles unless demonstrated by benchmarked regressions and migration playbooks
research_methods: 30-minute buyer interviews (target: platform engineering, procurement, security) — 12 interviews
Analysis of closed-won/closed-lost deals from CRM (last 18 months) to surface recurring objections
Field shadowing with 2 AE-led demos and 1 enterprise negotiation
Survey of 120 active trials to quantify top friction points
Synthesis workshop with sales, solutions engineering, and legal
data_sources: Zendesk: top support tickets during pilot phase
Console telemetry: first-week latency and error rates for trial accounts
Contracts: redlines requested by legal/security teams
Customer interviews and recorded demo notes
deliverables: Adoption barriers x seller interventions matrix (spreadsheet + condensed slide)
Field cheat-sheet for AEs (1 page) and POC template for SEs
Artifact library: SLA language snippets, KYC/KMS checklist, quantization regression summary
Presentation to GTM and Product Council (30 min + Q&A)
acceptance_criteria: 6 scenarios with supporting evidence (interview citations or CRM examples)
Seller interventions matrix prioritized by expected lift and implementation cost
AE cheat-sheet validated by at least 3 AE pilots and updated from feedback
Artifact library contains at least 3 reusable items (SLA template, security checklist, POC template)
Presentation scheduled and slides posted to Confluence with stakeholder sign-off
risks: Recruiting bias in interviews (over-index on strategic accounts)
CRM reasons may be inconsistently populated, limiting signal quality
Legal or security constraints could lengthen time to create reusable artifacts
Deliverables may require cross-team engineering work (instrumentation, dashboards) that is outside scope
